question: Find every place that PRESENTS a recorded/frozen/historical value but actually COMPUTES it live, starting from the confirmed instance in tools/perf_budget.py.

method.empirical: tools/perf_budget.py --check was executed 4 times to establish whether the 'historical' block's values are stable and equal to the committed artifact.
method.coverage_limit: A static search cannot PROVE absence of the pattern. It bounds the search: within the files opened and the tokens grepped, the ONLY construct that presents a recorded/frozen/historical value while computing it live is the perf_budget `historical` block. Files listed as grep-only were not read line-by-line.

anchor_confirmed_instance.code_reason: The block note says 'the recorded verdicts are preserved verbatim and must never be rewritten' (lines 245-246) and the module comment says the 343,547 literal is 'preserved verbatim and is still emitted' (lines 32-33). But the block is built as [... for r in advisory] taking r['value'], and every advisory row's value comes from a live measurement earlier in main(): context_bytes_per_artefact from worst = max(sizes.values()) (line 202-203), and the timing rows from perf_counter deltas (lines 176-199). Nothing here reads .hgk/artifacts/s2/PERF_BUDGET.json or BYTES_PER_ATOM_BASELINE.json to recover the recorded number.

frozen_counterpart_secondary.note: read correctly for the regression baseline (line 219) but the row field pi_bytes at line 217 is set from the LIVE sizes['pi'], not from this stored pi_bytes.

measured_evidence.honest_reading: On THIS checkout the context_bytes_per_artefact value is deterministic and happens to equal the recorded 343547 (artefact size is a function of the source spec, and the committed artifact was regenerated 2026-10-10 13:43). The parent brief's claim that two runs printed 366299 and 365351 did NOT reproduce here (4 runs printed 343547). The DEMONSTRABLY drifting rows are the three timing rows, which differ from the committed record on every run.

blast_radius.why_it_cannot_catch_drift: The guard hardcodes the value 343547 as its input (line 67) and the end-to-end test only asserts the METRIC NAME appears in preserved_fails (line 108) - it never reads the committed value 343547 nor pins the emitted number to it. Any large live value still yields verdict FAIL and preserved_fails==['context_bytes_per_artefact'], so the test passes while the emitted record drifts.

blast_radius.why: The ruling asserts the recorded FAIL 'is measured, printed and never rewritten' and the block note says the recorded verdicts are 'preserved verbatim'. A reader or gate taking historical.rows as the frozen record is misled whenever the live measurement differs.
The disclosure list item 'the historical FAIL was not rewritten' is only half-true: the verdict is not rewritten, but the underlying measured value is regenerated, not preserved.

anchor_confirmed_instance.severity_reason: It can make an acceptance claim FALSE: the owner ruling S2_HISTORICAL_FAIL: PRESERVE and the tool's own note both assert a recorded value is preserved verbatim, while the emitted value is a fresh measurement.

It is not a live-computed value (the opposite failure class: a frozen narrative that can go stale), so it is NOT a confirmed instance - but it is a recorded-claim the reader cannot re-derive.
A hard-coded denominator presented in the acceptance MD; not live-computed, not a provenance/live confusion. LOW.
A hard-coded frozen-candidate SHA emitted as if bound, while the release decisions ARE re-derived from file bytes. The field is static, not computed-live, so not an instance; note only.
